backup.production_rule: Five additive nullable columns on calendar_events (block_reason, block_reason_source, block_note, block_answered_by, block_answered_at; CHECKs only on the first three) and one on ops_notices (source, backfilled from the title and who entered it, then CHECKed socoteco/ngcp/staff). Two new service_role-only functions (telegram_answer_calendar_block_v2, telegram_note_calendar_block_v1). telegram_answer_calendar_block_v1 becomes a wrapper over v2 (live md5(prosrc) 7f43ea5dda50f325487aaa9ca04e473c, read 2026-10-05, equals 20260925010000). get_hospitality_metrics_v1 is replaced by the production body (live md5(prosrc) 0c2bc9aea7cdb418fb646590a2434a76, read 2026-10-05, equals 20260913100000) with one added predicate in the v_blocked query; the migration stops itself if either live md5 differs. No data is deleted, no table or grant is removed. restore_point and verified_at are placeholders: take a fresh backup, then fill both. Take a fresh backup if the one named is more than an hour old at apply time.

forward_verification.name: five_block_columns_on_calendar_events
forward_verification.query: select count(*) = 5 from information_schema.columns where table_schema = 'public' and table_name = 'calendar_events' and column_name in ('block_reason','block_reason_source','block_note','block_answered_by','block_answered_at')

forward_verification.name: v2_and_note_service_role_only
forward_verification.query: select has_function_privilege('service_role','public.telegram_answer_calendar_block_v2(bigint,text,text)','execute') and has_function_privilege('service_role','public.telegram_note_calendar_block_v1(bigint,text,text)','execute') and not has_function_privilege('authenticated','public.telegram_answer_calendar_block_v2(bigint,text,text)','execute') and not has_function_privilege('anon','public.telegram_answer_calendar_block_v2(bigint,text,text)','execute') and not has_function_privilege('authenticated','public.telegram_note_calendar_block_v1(bigint,text,text)','execute') and not has_function_privilege('anon','public.telegram_note_calendar_block_v1(bigint,text,text)','execute')

forward_verification.name: metrics_count_only_pending_blocks_and_body_is_the_reviewed_one
forward_verification.query: select pg_get_functiondef('public.get_hospitality_metrics_v1(uuid,date,date)'::regprocedure) like '%''pending'') = ''pending''%' and (select md5(replace(prosrc, chr(13), '')) from pg_proc where oid = 'public.get_hospitality_metrics_v1(uuid,date,date)'::regprocedure) = '36783f8532b14960e1563acba000d104'

forward_verification.name: ops_notices_source_checked_and_no_brownout_notice_without_one
forward_verification.query: select (select count(*) = 0 from public.ops_notices where notice_type = 'brownout' and source is null) and (select pg_get_constraintdef(oid) like '%socoteco%' and pg_get_constraintdef(oid) like '%ngcp%' and pg_get_constraintdef(oid) like '%staff%' from pg_constraint where conrelid = 'public.ops_notices'::regclass and conname = 'ops_notices_source_check')

forward_verification.name: pending_kinds_unchanged_awaiting_reply_carries_the_block_flows
forward_verification.query: select pg_get_constraintdef(oid) like '%awaiting_reply%' and pg_get_constraintdef(oid) like '%guest_save%' and pg_get_constraintdef(oid) not like '%block%' from pg_constraint where conrelid = 'public.telegram_pending'::regclass and conname = 'telegram_pending_kind_check'

steps.name: run_compensating_script
steps.action: Redeploy the previous calendar-sync and telegram-expense first (the cb:block tap calls v2 once this release is on), then apply supabase/rollbacks/20261005_calendar_block_triage.sql with run-sql-on-host.sh: it restores the pre-release bodies of telegram_answer_calendar_block_v1 and get_hospitality_metrics_v1 (asserting both md5s) and drops v2 and the note function. The columns stay: they are additive and hold the answers people gave.

feature_flags.name: sql_then_functions
feature_flags.required_state: Apply this release BEFORE deploying calendar-sync v16, telegram-expense (cb:block v2 and the two follow-up flows, pw:keep, noticeSource) and power-watch (source on its notice insert, auto-release). Deploying first is not safe: calendar-sync selects the new columns and telegram-expense calls the v2 rpc, both of which fail until it is applied. A brownout notice typed between the apply and the telegram-expense deploy has a null source: power-watch reads that as socoteco, and the null-source forward check (6) must be re-run after the deploys.
